evidence_rule: data.json carries an explicit age per record. A gap where the later age continues the earlier one is one man coming back; a gap where it jumps is two men. An age outside 17-45 is the same finding by another route: that row carries someone else's birth date. A gap with no age on either side is treated as a split until someone checks it, since printing the wrong man's name costs more than losing a factoid.

fields.career_incomplete: one man, confirmed, whose seasons this data does not all hold: his seasons rank and his gap is not a second man, but the running total under his name is not his career, so no career-level claim may use it
fields.confirmed: a human has checked this entry; false means the engine stays cautious
fields.evidence: what the data says, from the age rule below
fields.people: one block per person, oldest first; display_name null means the name is unknown
fields.split: true when the key covers more than one player

readme: One entry per name that data.json files under a single key but that may cover more than one player. Read by scripts/factoids.py only: build_data.py and data.json do not know this file exists. Candidates are names whose career has a gap longer than 4 seasons. split: true means two people, split: false means one player who came back after a spell away. confirmed says a human has checked the entry. An unconfirmed split holds back every season in an earlier segment, as a subject and as a previous holder, so no sentence carries the wrong man's name. A confirmed split prints each segment's own display_name and counts each segment as its own man, so "his own mark" never reaches across the two; a segment whose display_name is null is a man whose name is not known and stays held back. Career-level claims stay closed for every split key either way, because career_earnings on a merged record sums two men. An unconfirmed split: false entry keeps the career-level exclusion its gap triggered: a long gap under one name is not proof of one person. Confirming it is what lets the name rank as one career. career_incomplete is the one case where confirming does not open career claims: one man, checked, whose seasons this data does not all hold, so the running total under his name is a part of a career rather than a career. Four entries were removed once the build began joining on a person: Brandon Williams, Chris Smith, Gerald Henderson and Jaren Jackson Jr each covered two men under one key, and each father now has his own name and his own records, so there is nothing left for an entry to split. Corey Brewer is the one key still covering two men, because bio.csv has a row for only one of them.
